title: Certified spin, mass and horizons of the Bowen-York spinning puncture family
description:
In plain words. The Bowen-York construction is a common way to set up a spinning black hole on a computer. Numerical work pointed to a ceiling on its spin ratio J/M^2 near 0.928. We proved where the ceiling is, with interval arithmetic that carries a guaranteed error bar on every number, and proved several facts about the family by hand.

Results (computer-assisted where stated). For the single, non-boosted, conformally flat, maximal Bowen-York spinning puncture with bare mass mu > 0: two-sided certified ADM mass enclosures for every spin parameter up to j = 11994.8 and a one-sided bound beyond; the supremum of J/M_ADM^2 over the family lies in [0.9282004538, 0.9282004687], so it rounds to 0.928200 (decision blind-replicated). At fixed J ≠ 0 the mass M(mu) is strictly increasing (a corollary of Dain and Gabach Clement's Lemmas 3.1-3.2, which we record), strictly convex and C^1; the supremum is not attained and equals the spin of the extreme (mu = 0) data, certified directly on the throat: chi(0) in [0.92820045875619, 0.92820045878266] (blind-replicated). A mass formula for the extreme data from its throat profile alone, M_0 = (2/3) Sum (2l+1) a_l^2, a Lichnerowicz analogue of the radial Pohozaev invariant of Korevaar, Mazzeo, Pacard and Schoen. For mu > 0 the throat is the only closed connected MOTS and minimal surface. The extreme data contain no closed minimal surface, MOTS or apparent horizon, answering a question Dain and Gabach Clement left open; two independent proofs (the sliding method of Berestycki and Nirenberg is credited).

Checks. 17 sealed tests (16 HOLD, 1 FAILED and re-tested), blind independent replications, internal hostile referee reports (internal lab checks, not external peer review), and a clean-room reproduction from the repository. Limitations are listed in Section 11 of the paper.

Open doors. Dain and Gabach Clement (2009) conjectured that a small perturbation of extreme Bowen-York data always has a horizon; we proved the companion statement that the extreme data themselves have none, and we found no later answer to the conjecture (search of 2026-11-17). The exponent with which the spin approaches its ceiling (our Conjecture E) is a heuristic that agrees with one sealed numerical check but is unproved. A sharp, certified area-spin constant for the family (probe value about 1.1991) was not found in our search to 2026-11-17 and is not certified here. The one-sphere mass formula of Section 7 appears to extend to maximally sliced spinning trumpet data; we did not test this.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
